Hundreds of Dimona residents whose homes were damaged by an Iranian missile strike gathered Saturday night at a nearby school, where they registered for assistance and, if unable to return to their damaged home, were evacuated to hotels. A total of 59 people were injured in the strike, most of them lightly, and were taken to Soroka Medical Center. The strike in Dimona, which left dozens of people wounded, including a child in serious condition, occurred after an interceptor was launched toward the missile but is believed to have missed. articles.title: Iran denies role in reported missile attempt on Diego Garcia as US weighs ground invasion options
articles.lede: Iran on Sunday [Local Time] denied targeting the UK's military base on Diego Garcia, with a senior official telling Al Jazeera that Tehran was not behind the reported missile attempt. The denial comes after a report by The Wall Street Journal claimed that Iran fired two intermediate-range ballistic missiles towards the joint US-UK military base in the Chagos Archipelago. However, one missile failed during flight, while the other was likely intercepted. The report did not specify when the missiles were fired. Diego Garcia lies about 4,000 kilometres from Iran, and the reported strike attempt, now denied by Tehran as per the Al Jazeera report, would have raised questions about the actual range of Iran's missile capabilities, which the country has publicly said is limited. articles.title: Paramedics treat nearly 100 people after Iranian missile hits Arad in southern Israel
articles.lede: Paramedics treat nearly 100 people after Iranian missile hits Arad in southern Israel. "A blatant war crime. Pure terrorism," the Israeli Foreign Ministry said. United Hatzalah said that its paramedics treated 95 patients, including 10 in serious condition and some who were hospitalized, after a "mass casualty incident" in Arad, in southern Israel, some 25 miles east of Be'er Sheva. The Israeli Foreign Ministry called the attack on Arad and one earlier in the day on Dimona a "blatant war crime" and "pure terrorism." Aerial footage that United Hatzalah posted appeared to show a large area in which the missile impacted, including blown-out residential buildings.
